landmarks.name: Pyramids of Meroë
landmarks.writeup: Ancient Nubian pyramids located in the northeastern region, showcasing the Kingdom of Kush's rich history.

wiki.extract: Meroë was an ancient city on the east bank of the Nile about 6 km north-east of the Kabushiya station near Shendi, Sudan, approximately 200 km north-east of Khartoum. Near the site is a group of villages called Bagrawiyah. This city was the capital of the Kingdom of Kush for several centuries from around 590 BC, until its collapse in the 4th century AD. The Kushitic Kingdom of Meroë gave its name to the "Island of Meroë", which was the modern region of Butana, a region bounded by the Nile, the Atbarah and the Blue Nile.

landmarks.name: Jebel Barkal
landmarks.writeup: A small mountain considered sacred, surrounded by archaeological sites linked to the ancient Kingdom of Napata.

wiki.extract: Jebel Barkal or Gebel Barkal is a mesa located 400 km north of Khartoum, next to Karima in Northern State in Sudan, and near the Nile River in Nubia. The Jebel is 104 meters tall, has a flat top, and came to have religious significance for both ancient Kush and ancient Egyptian occupiers. In 2003, the mountain, together with the extensive archaeological site at its base, were named as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO. The area houses the Jebel Barkal Museum.

landmarks.name: Suakin Island
landmarks.writeup: Historic Red Sea port with Ottoman-era ruins reflecting Sudan's maritime trade history.

wiki.extract: Suakin or Sawakin is a port city in northeastern Sudan, on the west coast of the Red Sea. It was formerly the region's chief port, but is now secondary to Port Sudan, about 50 kilometres (30 mi) north.

cultural_events.name: Sufi Festivals
cultural_events.writeup: Religious gatherings featuring traditional music and dance, celebrating Sudan's Sufi Islamic heritage.

wiki.extract: Sufism or Sufi Islam is a mystic body of religious practice found within Islam that is characterized by a focus on Islamic purification, spirituality, ritualism, and asceticism.

cultural_events.name: Khartoum International Book Fair
cultural_events.writeup: Annual event promoting literature and cultural exchange in Sudan.

wiki.extract: Muhammad Taha Al-Qaddal, also transcribed as Muhammad Al-Gaddal, was a Sudanese poet. Al-Qaddal began his literary career in the late 1960s; he wrote contemporary Arabic lyric poetry and became known in the early 1980s for expressing socio-political messages through his verses. Some of his poems were put to music by some Sudanese singers. His poetry was about the suffering of Sudanese during the late 1990s Islamist military government period.

food_writeup: Sudanese cuisine blends Arab and African influences, featuring dishes like ful medames (stewed fava beans), kisra (fermented bread), and tagine-style stews with meat and vegetables.
brief_history: Sudan has a history dating back to ancient Nubian kingdoms. It was colonized by the British and Egyptians in the 19th century and gained independence in 1956. The country has experienced civil wars, the secession of South Sudan in 2011, and ongoing political transitions.

important_people.name: Omar al-Bashir
important_people.description: Former president who ruled from 1989 to 2019

important_people.name: Sadiq al-Mahdi
important_people.description: Former Prime Minister and opposition leader

current_conflicts: Sudan faces internal conflicts including clashes in Darfur, South Kordofan, and Blue Nile regions, as well as political instability following the 2019 revolution.
